text.en: Imperative sentences are formed with a verb form that omits or lacks subject personal affixes ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-omits-subject-marking⟧. Interjections such as *hokure* and *hetak* frequently introduce imperative sentences ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--interjections-introducing-imperatives⟧. The markers *yan*, *ro*, and *na* are sentence-final elements associated with imperative sentences ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--sentence-final-suffixes-in-imperatives⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the final particle *koh* forms an imperative restricted to social inferiors such as children ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--sakhalin-koh-downward-imperative⟧.
text.ja: 命令文は動詞に主格人称接辞が付かない、あるいは主語要素を欠いた動詞形によって形成される⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-omits-subject-marking⟧。*hokure*や*hetak*などの感嘆詞が命令文を導くことが頻繁にある⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--interjections-introducing-imperatives⟧。*yan*、*ro*、*na*は命令文に関連する文末要素である⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--sentence-final-suffixes-in-imperatives⟧。樺太アイヌ語では、終助詞*koh*が子どもなど目下の者に制限された命令形を形成する⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--sakhalin-koh-downward-imperative⟧。

text.en: An imperative addressed to a single addressee is formed with a verb lacking subject personal affixes ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--singular-imperative-formed-by-bare-verb⟧. A verb form lacking subject affixes is formally ambiguous between a singular imperative addressed to the second person and a third-person declarative clause ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--singular-imperative-ambiguous-with-third-person⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu imperative sentences, the clause-final syllable is normally pronounced high and long, distinguishing them prosodically from declarative sentences ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-intonation-high-and-long⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, the singular imperative is expressed by the bare verb stem uttered with terminal rising intonation ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--singular-imperative-bare-stem-sakhalin⟧. Imperatives formed by using the bare verb carry a rough or hasty nuance ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--bare-imperative-rough-or-hasty-nuance⟧. In the Ishikari dialect, the sentence-final particle *ya* attaches to singular verb forms to mark a singular imperative ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--ishikari-particle-ya-singular-imperative⟧. The particle *ora* appears to function to emphasize commands ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--particle-ora-emphasizes-imperatives⟧. In Shizunai, transitive verbs that normally require an overt object may occasionally occur without an object in imperative clauses ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-transitive-verbs-object-omission⟧.
text.ja: 単数の相手に対する命令文は、動詞に主格人称接辞を欠く形によって形成される⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--singular-imperative-formed-by-bare-verb⟧。主格接辞を欠く動詞形は、形式上、二人称への単数命令文か三人称主語の平叙文かの区別がつかず文脈に依存する⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--singular-imperative-ambiguous-with-third-person⟧。北海道アイヌ語の命令文では文末の音節が高く長く発音されるのが通例であり、イントネーションによって平叙文と区別される⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-intonation-high-and-long⟧。樺太アイヌ語において単数の相手に対する命令は、動詞語幹をそのまま文末を上昇調で発音することによって表される⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--singular-imperative-bare-stem-sakhalin⟧。動詞を単独で用いる命令文には、ぞんざい、あるいは性急な命令というニュアンスがある⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--bare-imperative-rough-or-hasty-nuance⟧。石狩方言では、動詞単数形に終助詞*ya*を後続させて単数命令を表す⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--ishikari-particle-ya-singular-imperative⟧。助詞*ora*は命令を強調する機能を持つようである⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--particle-ora-emphasizes-imperatives⟧。静内方言において、通常は目的語を必要とする他動詞であっても命令節では目的語なしで現れることがある⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-transitive-verbs-object-omission⟧。

text.en: The sentence-final particle *yan* marks polite commands, being used for plural addressees and also for polite directives addressed to a single person ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-polite-imperative-marker⟧⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-plural-and-polite-singular-command⟧. When the addressee is plural, a plural verb stem cannot be used alone as an imperative, and *yan* is obligatory, attaching to the plural verb stem if the verb distinguishes number ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-with-plural-verb-stem⟧⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--plural-imperative-requires-yan⟧. As a rule, *hani* is used for singular commands while *yan* is used for plural commands, but *yan* can be polite singular and *yan hani* plural polite ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--hani-singular-yan-plural-distribution⟧. Satō proposes that *yan* is underlyingly a plural addressee marker, deriving its polite nuance toward a single addressee pragmatically through indirectness ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-politeness-derived-from-plurality⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, the final particle *yan* may indicate either a plural subject or a plural object in an imperative predicate ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--shizunai-yan-plural-subject-or-object⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the imperative particle *yan* may take the allomorphic shape *an* following a consonant ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-alternates-to-an-after-consonant⟧.
text.ja: 終助詞*yan*は丁寧な命令の標識として機能し、複数の相手に対する命令のほか、単数の相手に対する丁寧な命令にも用いられる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-polite-imperative-marker⟧⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-plural-and-polite-singular-command⟧。命令の対象が複数の場合、複数形語幹単独で命令文を形成することはできず*yan*の付加が必須であり、動詞が単複を区別する際には複数形語幹に*yan*が後続する⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-with-plural-verb-stem⟧⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--plural-imperative-requires-yan⟧。原則として命令助詞には単数に*hani*、複数に*yan*が用いられるが、丁寧表現では単数に*yan*、複数に*yan hani*も用いられる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--hani-singular-yan-plural-distribution⟧。佐藤は、*yan*が本来的には複数命令の形式であり、単数に転用されることで間接性により丁寧さを表すようになったと提起している⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-politeness-derived-from-plurality⟧。静内方言において終助詞*yan*は、命令述語において複数主語または複数目的語を表すことができる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--shizunai-yan-plural-subject-or-object⟧。北海道アイヌ語において命令助詞*yan*は、子音の後で異形態*an*をとることがある⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yan-alternates-to-an-after-consonant⟧。

text.en: The sentence-final particle *hani* can be added to an imperative to soften the tone and provide reassurance or urging ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--particle-hani-softens-imperative⟧. Following a consonant, *hani* often loses initial *h* and takes the form *ani* ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--particle-hani-alternates-to-ani⟧. In southwestern Hokkaido, the verb sequence *wa pirka* functions as a polite directive construction ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--wa-pirka-polite-imperative⟧. Adding a benefactive imperative auxiliary like *wa en=kore* expresses a polite request rather than a plain command ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--benefactive-wa-kore-forms-polite-request⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the auxiliary collocation *wa kore* is used exclusively in directive expressions and does not appear in declarative clauses ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--wa-kore-restricted-to-imperatives⟧.
text.ja: 命令文末に終助詞*hani*を付加することで、口調を和らげ念を押すようなニュアンスを添えることができる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--particle-hani-softens-imperative⟧。終助詞*hani*は子音の後で語頭の*h*が脱落して*ani*の形をとることが多い⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--particle-hani-alternates-to-ani⟧。北海道南西部方言において動詞連続構文*wa pirka*は丁寧な命令構文として機能する⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--wa-pirka-polite-imperative⟧。*wa en=kore*などの授与補助動詞を後続させることで、平易な命令よりも丁寧な依頼を表す⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--benefactive-wa-kore-forms-polite-request⟧。北海道アイヌ語において補助動詞的連語*wa kore*は命令表現でのみ用いられ、平叙文には現れない⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--wa-kore-restricted-to-imperatives⟧。

text.en: Proper imperative verb forms are restricted in usage to direct speech and main clauses ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-proper-restricted-to-direct-speech⟧. Mild imperatives can be formed using elements such as *nankor*, *kus-ne*, and *kuni-p* ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--mild-imperative-particles-kindaichi-chiri⟧. Modal constructions such as *yak pirka*, *kusu ne na*, *p ne na*, and *nankor na* convey imperative meanings when used with second-person subjects, requiring subject personal affixes ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--modal-expressions-with-second-person-convey-imperative⟧. A verb inflected for a second-person subject followed by *kusu ne na* expresses an imperative or directive meaning ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--indirect-imperatives-with-kusu-ne-na⟧. In the Saru dialect, the construction *eci-... kusu ne na* functions as a directive addressed to second-person plural subjects ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--saru-eci-kusu-ne-na-plural-directive⟧. The particle sequence *nankor na* takes on an imperative meaning specifically when used with the second person ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--nankor-na-imperative-meaning-second-person⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the conditional construction *yak pirka* ('it is good if...') is frequently used with an imperative sense ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yak-pirka-imperative-use⟧. Satō proposes that constructions using second-person subject personal affixes, such as *kusu ne na* or *yak pirka*, serve as admonitions or indirect directives rather than simple bare imperatives ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--second-person-constructions-as-mitigated-admonition⟧. In Sakhalin Ainu, request forms are formed by verb-final particles *kanne*, *waa*, and *koh*, descending in politeness in that order ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--sakhalin-request-final-particles⟧.
text.ja: 本来の命令動詞形式の使用は直接話法および主節に限定される⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-proper-restricted-to-direct-speech⟧。柔らかな命令には*nankor*、*kus-ne*、*kuni-p*などの要素が用いられる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--mild-imperative-particles-kindaichi-chiri⟧。*yak pirka*、*kusu ne na*、*p ne na*、*nankor na*などのモダリティ構文は、二人称主語で用いられるときに命令の意味を表すが、主格人称接辞を必要とする⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--modal-expressions-with-second-person-convey-imperative⟧。二人称主格の人称接辞が付いた動詞に*kusu ne na*が後続することで命令的・指示的意味を表す⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--indirect-imperatives-with-kusu-ne-na⟧。沙流方言において*eci-... kusu ne na*構文は二人称複数に対する命令表現として機能する⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--saru-eci-kusu-ne-na-plural-directive⟧。不変化詞連続*nankor na*は二人称とともに用いられた場合に命令の意味を表す⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--nankor-na-imperative-meaning-second-person⟧。北海道アイヌ語において条件構文*yak pirka*（「〜すると良い」）は命令的な意味で頻繁に用いられる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--yak-pirka-imperative-use⟧。佐藤は、*kusu ne na*や*yak pirka*など二人称主格接辞を用いる構文が、単純な命令というより教え諭すような間接的命令を表すと提起している⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--second-person-constructions-as-mitigated-admonition⟧。樺太アイヌ語では動詞終助詞*kanne*、*waa*、*koh*によって依頼形が形成され、丁寧度はこの順に低くなる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--sakhalin-request-final-particles⟧。

text.en: In the imperative, verbs lack subject person-and-number marking but must take object person marking when transitive ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-verb-unmarked-for-subject-marked-for-object⟧. Affixing a second-person subject prefix to a verb to form an imperative is ungrammatical ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-second-person-prefix-ungrammatical⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, imperative forms never take subject personal affixes, standing as an exception to the general rule of obligatory subject marking on verbs ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-lacks-subject-affix-as-exception⟧. The imperative does not take second-person nominative affixes because the argument slot is pragmatically satisfied by imperative modality ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-subject-slot-pragmatically-satisfied⟧. In Shizunai Ainu, imperative sentences are characterized by the omission of the verbal nominative pronominal affix ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--shizunai-imperative-drops-pronominal-affix⟧. In Hokkaido Ainu, the independent second-person pronoun *eani* is attested in an imperative sentence, but this usage is extremely rare ⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--independent-pronoun-eani-rare-in-imperative⟧.
text.ja: 命令法において動詞は主語の人称・数標示を受けないが、他動詞である場合には目的語の人称接辞が付される⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-verb-unmarked-for-subject-marked-for-object⟧。二人称主格接辞を動詞に付けて命令文を作ることは文法的に認められない⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-second-person-prefix-ungrammatical⟧。北海道アイヌ語において命令形は主格人称接辞を決して取らず、動詞に主格人称接辞が必須であるという原則の例外となっている⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-lacks-subject-affix-as-exception⟧。アイヌ語の命令形が二人称主格接辞を取らないのは、命令というモダリティにより項スロットが語用論的に充足されるためである⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--imperative-subject-slot-pragmatically-satisfied⟧。静内方言において命令文は動詞の主格代名詞接辞が脱落することによって特徴づけられる⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--shizunai-imperative-drops-pronominal-affix⟧。北海道アイヌ語において命令文中に独立二人称代名詞*eani*が用いられる実例はあるものの、この用法は極めて稀である⟦claim:tam/imperative-and-prohibitive--independent-pronoun-eani-rare-in-imperative⟧。
